main.content:
==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|En-au-run over.ogg|a=AU}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|<,,ran,run>}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|idiomatic}} To [[exceed]] the allotted time.
#: {{syn|en|overrun#Verb<qq:intransitive>}}
#: {{ux|en|The previous presentation '''ran over''' and ours had to start late.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cross by running.
#: {{ux|en|The athletes must '''run over''' the bridge to reach the finish line.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|idiomatic}} To [[drive]] over, causing injury or death.
#: {{syn|en|overrun#Verb<qq:transitive>}}
#: {{ux|en|Can you believe somebody would just '''run over''' a cat like that?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|by extension}} To [[mistreat]] out of [[disregard]].
#: {{syn|en|overrun#Verb<qq:transitive>}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|idiomatic}} To describe briefly; to [[summarize]] or [[recapitulate]]; to go through or consider quickly.
#: {{ux|en|Before we start the project, let's just '''run over''' who is doing what.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|idiomatic}} To [[rehearse]] quickly.
#: {{ux|en|You'd better '''run over''' your statement before going on the platform.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[overflow]].
#: {{syn|en|overrun#Verb<qq:intransitive>}}
#: {{ux|en|The bath water nearly '''ran over'''.}}
# {{lb|en|rugby}} To score a [[try]].
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|date=December 31, 2010
|author=
|title=Magners League: Cardiff Blues 27-25 Osprey
|work=BBC
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/rugby_union/welsh/9326565.stm
|page=
|passage=Andrew Bishop then '''ran over''' in the closing stages, but it was too late.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123200847/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/rugby_union/welsh/9326565.stm|archivedate=23 January 2022}}
# {{lb|en|engineering}} To have rotation in such direction that the crank pin traverses the upper, or front, half of its path in the forward, or outward, stroke; said of a crank which drives, or is driven by, a reciprocating piece.

====Usage notes====
* The verb and the particle are generally inseparable, even when the object is a pronoun.
** However, in the sense of "to drive over" (a thing or person), the pair is often separated: ''He didn't see the raccoon in time to brake, and sadly he '''ran''' it '''over'''''; or, ''He didn't see the raccoon in time to brake, and sadly he '''ran over''' it''.
